disposition: deferred: sym_recall .1536 and sym_precision .1705 collapse far below the L1 good floor (.95/.90 for tool formats), but this is not a doc.json selector gap — every required kind is emitted (fathom_defs 2152 vs oracle_defs 2390 are close in magnitude; the shortfall is almost entirely name KEY-matching, not missing/extra entities). Root cause, confirmed directly with a reverted-before-commit experiment (internal/langbench/score.go's BareName forced to identity, then reverted): matched jumps from 367/2390 to 1991/2390 (babel alone: 13/1638 -> 1637/1638, sym_recall .0079 -> .9994, L1 excellent). BareName() strips a name's text after the last '.'/':'/'#'/'/'/'\\'/' '/')' -- a convention built for programming-language qualification (Class.method) that collides with THREE separate, common npm conventions this dialect's own required and non-required kinds legitimately produce: (1) scoped package names, BareName("@babel/core")="core" -- every scoped package (the overwhelming majority in both subjects) loses its scope and collides with every other package sharing that last segment; (2) colon-namespaced script names, BareName("codesandbox:build")="build", BareName("test:esm")="esm" -- an extremely common npm convention (build:watch, test:e2e, lint:fix); (3) export subpaths, BareName("./utils")="utils", and BareName(".")="" (the root subpath becomes the empty string) -- while npm's own names (the oracle, via `npm pkg get`, tier A) are never BareName'd, so almost no scoped-package/colon-script/subpath-export name can key-match its oracle counterpart before line-distance is even considered. This is the same class of gap CSS's reading root-caused (LB-Q-css-rest: BareName's separator set colliding with that dialect's own domain punctuation) manifesting through '/' and ':' instead of '.'/'#'/':'. Neither fix belongs to this dialect: BareName is a cross-cutting internal/langbench primitive shared by every already-measured dialect (an Opus-reviewed change, design §15), and there is no query or entity change in doc.json that can make a package's own published name stop containing '/' or a script's own name stop containing ':'. Separately, and much smaller: a `bin`/`exports` field written as a single string rather than an object (real in both subjects, e.g. next's own `"bin": "dist/bin/next"`-style packages) is not captured as its own entity at all -- the doc-engine's selectors are evaluated relative to the matched node with no path back to a sibling `name` field, so there is no name to give such an entity; disclosed, not query-fixable without a doc-engine capability change (also not a worker's file). L2's ref_recall/ref_precision and L3's xref_precision/xref_recall are separately unreachable: package.json has no intra-file entity-to-entity reference this engine's selector model can express (scripts/bin/exports don't reference each other structurally, only by convention in string command text), so FamilyRefs is never measured (not-attempted, correctly -- forcing a fake reference to pass the metric is exactly what design §14.2 rules out); and xref_precision/xref_recall have no scoring implementation at all in cmd/indexbench/langoracle.go or internal/langbench/merge.go (no FamilyXref constant, no CntXref* counts, and BenchExtraction never carries DocResult.CrossFile through the generic Extractor interface DocExtractor.Extract narrows to) even though the metric names exist in reading.go's threshold table -- confirmed directly by reading both files; this dialect's doc.json still declares real cross_file selectors (workspace-member globs, dependency/devDependency/peerDependency/optionalDependency edges via module-source) so that plumbing is ready the moment a foundation change wires it through. LB-Q-package-json stays unchecked; see LB-Q-package-json-rest. Trigger: an Opus-reviewed internal/langbench change gives BareName a per-canonical-kind (or dialect-declared) policy so '/' and ':' are not treated as qualification separators for package/task/route kinds, then package-json.json is re-measured; independently, an Opus-reviewed foundation change adds a NotApplicable-style carve-out (or a genuine metric) for a tool format with no intra-file reference concept, and another wires DocResult.CrossFile through BenchExtraction plus FamilyXref/CntXref* scoring so L3 becomes measurable at all for any doc-engine dialect, not only this one.
